The following provides a quick overview of the main components and their interactions.

**`Main`** (consisting of classes [`Main`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W09-4/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/insureconnect/Main.java) and [`MainApp`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W09-4/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/insureconnect/MainApp.java)) is in charge of the app launch and shut down.
* At app launch, it initializes the other components in the correct sequence, and connects them up with each other.
* At shut down, it shuts down the other components and invokes cleanup methods where necessary.
The bulk of the app's work is done by the following four components:
* [**`Model`**](#model-component): Holds the data of the App in memory.
* [**`Storage`**](#storage-component): Reads data from, and writes data to, the hard disk.
[**`Commons`**](#common-classes) represents a collection of classes used by multiple other components.
**How the architecture components interact with each other**
The *Sequence Diagram* below shows how the components interact with each other for the scenario where the user issues the command `delete 1`.
Each of the four main components (also shown in the diagram above),
* defines its *API* in an `interface` with the same name as the Component.
* provides its functionality through a concrete `{Component Name}Manager` class that implements the corresponding API interface.

For example, the `Logic` component defines its API in `Logic.java` and implements it in `LogicManager.java`. Other components interact with a component through its interface rather than its concrete class, preventing them from coupling to that component's implementation, as illustrated in the following partial class diagram.
The sections below give more details of each component.
The **API** of this component is specified in [`Ui.java`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W09-4/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/insureconnect/ui/Ui.java)

The UI consists of a `MainWindow` and its parts, such as `CommandBox`, `ResultDisplay`, `PersonListPanel`, and `CustomerDetailsPanel`. All of these, including `MainWindow`, inherit from the abstract `UiPart` class, which captures common behavior among classes that represent visible GUI parts. `CommandHistory`, `FocusNavigation`, and `ColourSchemeStyles` are helper classes that are not GUI parts, so they do not inherit from `UiPart`.
The sequence diagram below illustrates how the customer list and details panel remain synchronized when the selected customer changes.

When a customer is selected, `MainWindow` receives the selection change and asks `CustomerDetailsPanel` to display that customer's information. If the displayed list becomes empty, the selection becomes `null` and the details panel displays its empty state. If the selected customer is removed while other customers remain, `PersonListPanel` selects the nearest remaining customer.

The `UI` component uses the JavaFX UI framework. The layouts of these UI parts are defined in matching `.fxml` files in `src/main/resources/view`. For example, [`MainWindow.fxml`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W09-4/tp/tree/master/src/main/resources/view/MainWindow.fxml) specifies the layout of [`MainWindow`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W09-4/tp/tree/master/src/main/java/seedu/insureconnect/ui/MainWindow.java).
`MainWindow` opens the `HelpWindow` when the user enters `help`, selects the Help menu item, or presses F1.
The window shows the available command formats and a link to the User Guide with a **Copy URL** button.

This section describes some noteworthy details on how certain features are implemented.

`InsureConnectParser` sends an `edit` command to `EditCommandParser`. The parser reads the displayed-list index and the supplied prefixes, including `r/`, then creates an `EditPersonDescriptor`. A missing `r/` leaves the descriptor's remark as `null`, meaning that the existing remark should be kept. If `r/` is present without text, `ParserUtil.parseRemark` creates an empty `Remark`, meaning that the existing remark should be cleared. Remark input is trimmed, repeated whitespace is collapsed, and values longer than 500 characters after normalization are rejected. Duplicate `r/` prefixes are rejected.

`EditCommand` selects the customer by index from the current filtered list. It creates a replacement `Person` using the supplied descriptor values and retaining existing values for omitted fields, including the remark. The original creation time is retained. After checking for duplicate customers and policy numbers, the command replaces the person in the model and shows the full list. `LogicManager` saves the data when it has changed.

* is an insurance agent (or financial adviser) based in Singapore
* manages a large portfolio of customers (up to about 1000), each holding one or more insurance policies
* handles many policies, claims, renewals and follow-ups daily
* needs to pull up a customer's contact details and policy numbers quickly, for example while the customer is on the line
* finds it hard to remember customers' policy numbers, but remembers their names
* does most of their administrative work on a laptop or desktop computer
* can type fast and prefers typing to mouse interactions
* is reasonably comfortable using CLI apps

**Value proposition**: InsureConnect gives an insurance agent fast access to customer contact details and associated policy numbers through typed commands, so that a customer can be found by name instead of by a policy number that is hard to remember. It is faster than a spreadsheet or a mouse-driven CRM, keeps all data on the agent's own computer and works without an internet connection.

**Policy scope**: Policy numbers are identifiers attached to customer records. Searching by policy number retrieves matching customer records. InsureConnect does not store policy coverage, premiums, renewal dates or policy status, and remarks apply to a customer rather than an individual policy.

1.  Should work on any _mainstream OS_ as long as it has Java `25` or above installed.
2.  Should be able to hold up to 1000 customers without noticeable sluggishness in performance for typical usage.
3.  Should respond to any command within 2 seconds when holding up to 1000 customers.

4.  A user with above average typing speed for regular English text (i.e. not code, not system admin commands) should be able to accomplish most of the tasks faster using commands than using the mouse.
5.  Should be usable by a single user only; data is not shared between users or computers.
6.  Should store data locally in a human editable text file, so that an advanced user can inspect and correct the data without the app.
7.  Should not depend on a database management system or a remote server, and should work fully without an internet connection.

8.  Should save data to the hard disk after every command that changes data, so that no change is lost if the app is closed unexpectedly. If a save fails, the user should be told so in the result of that same command.
9.  Should never overwrite an existing data file that it failed to read.
10. Should be packaged as a single JAR file of no more than 100MB that runs without an installer.
11. The GUI should work well (i.e. no resolution related inconvenience) for screen resolutions 1920x1080 and higher, and screen scales 100% and 125%.
12. The GUI should remain usable (i.e. all functions can be used even if the experience is not optimal) for screen resolutions 1280x720 and higher, and screen scales 150%.
13. Every error message for an invalid command should state the expected command format or the accepted values, so that the user can correct the command without consulting the User Guide.
* **Mainstream OS**: Windows, Linux, Unix, or macOS
* **Agent**: An insurance agent or financial adviser who sells insurance policies and uses InsureConnect to manage their customers
* **Customer**: A person whose details are recorded in InsureConnect, who holds at least one insurance policy sold by the agent
* **Policy**: An insurance contract held by a customer, such as a life, health, motor or travel insurance plan

* **Policy number**: The unique code that identifies a policy, made up of 1 to 30 characters with at least one letter or digit; hyphens and slashes are also allowed (e.g. `LIFE-2026/SG`). Every customer has at least one, and no two customers can share the same policy number. Entered with the `t/` prefix

* **Remark**: An optional free text note attached to a customer, used for follow-ups and preferences (e.g. `Prefers WhatsApp after 6pm`). The `r/` prefix sets it, and `edit INDEX r/` clears it. An omitted remark is stored as an empty string when adding a customer

* **Duplicate customer**: A customer whose name and phone number match those of an existing customer. Name matching ignores case, extra spaces, and canonical Unicode differences (for example, precomposed and decomposed accents). Phone matching ignores a leading `+`; for Singapore numbers, the `65` country code is also ignored when comparing it with an 8-digit local number

* **Prefix matching**: The way `find` compares keywords with names: a keyword matches a name if any word in the name starts with the keyword, ignoring case (e.g. `Jane` matches `Mary-Jane Tan` and `wei` matches `Tan Wei Ming`, but `ei` does not)

* **Index**: The position number of a customer in the currently displayed list, used to identify the customer in commands such as `delete`. Indices start from 1 and change when the list is filtered by `find` or a customer is deleted
* **Prefix**: The short marker that comes before a value in a command, such as `n/` for name or `p/` for phone
* **Escape character**: A character (`!`) used within the `n/` name, `a/` address, and `r/` remark fields to prevent patterns (such as ` a/` or ` t/`) from being misinterpreted as command prefixes
* **Data file**: The JSON file in which InsureConnect stores all customer records on the user's computer
* **MSS**: Main Success Scenario, the most common sequence of steps in a use case when nothing goes wrong

InsureConnect is a **desktop application for managing contacts, optimized for use through a Command Line Interface (CLI)** while retaining the benefits of a Graphical User Interface (GUI). If you type quickly, InsureConnect can help you manage contacts faster than traditional GUI applications.

InsureConnect stores customer contact details and associated policy numbers. You can use a policy number to find its customer record. It does not store policy coverage, premiums, renewal dates or policy status; consult your insurer's records for these details. Remarks belong to the customer record, not to an individual policy.

* Words in `UPPER_CASE` are the parameters to be supplied by the user.
For example, in `add n/NAME`, replace `NAME` with a value such as `John Doe`.
* Items in square brackets are optional.
For example, `edit INDEX [n/NAME]` can be used as `edit 1 n/John Doe` or as `edit 1 p/98765432`.
* Items followed by `…`​ can appear zero or more times.
For example, `[t/POLICY_NUMBER]…​` in `edit` may be omitted, or written as `t/LIFE20481` or `t/LIFE20481 t/HEALTH20482`.
* Parameters can be in any order.
For example, if the command specifies `n/NAME p/PHONE_NUMBER`, `p/PHONE_NUMBER n/NAME` is also acceptable.

* **Name constraints**: `NAME` must start with a Latin-script letter or digit. It may contain Latin-script letters (including accented letters such as `é` and `ö`), combining accent marks, digits, spaces, and the characters `-`, `'`, `’`, `.`, `/`, and `!`. Names written in other scripts are not supported, and names cannot consist solely of punctuation (e.g. `---`, `...`, `///` are invalid).

* **Policy number constraints**: Each `t/POLICY_NUMBER` must be 1 to 30 characters long, contain at least one letter or digit, and may include hyphens (`-`) or slashes (`/`). Spaces and other punctuation are not allowed. Every customer needs at least one policy number, and a policy number can belong to only one customer. Policy numbers are case-insensitive and are displayed in uppercase. For example, life20481 and LIFE20481 refer to the same policy number.
* **Escape character (`!`) for name, address, and remark prefix collisions**:

Command prefixes are identified by a space followed by a letter and a slash (e.g. ` a/` for address, ` t/` for policy number). Names, addresses, or remarks that contain these patterns can conflict with command prefixes if typed directly.
To avoid prefix collisions, prefix the collision point with an exclamation mark `!` within the name, address, or remark field:
* `n/Mohd !a/l Kassim` or `n/Mohd a!/l Kassim` will be saved as `Mohd a/l Kassim`.
* Indian patronymics such as `s/o` or `d/o` (e.g. `n/Ravi s/o Muthu`) do not conflict with existing prefixes and do not require escaping (though `!s/o` is also supported).
* In a remark, `r/dietary restrictions: !n/a` will be saved as `dietary restrictions: n/a`.
* In an address, `a/Blk 123 !t/4` will be saved as `Blk 123 t/4`.
* If you need a literal exclamation mark in a name, address, or remark, type `!!` (for example, `a/Block!! A` is saved as `Block! A`).
* **Warning:** A single `!` before any character is treated as an escape marker and removed. For example, `r/Great! Thanks` is saved as `Great Thanks`.

* **Note:** `!` is treated as an escape character only in the name (`n/`), address (`a/`), and remark (`r/`) fields. Other fields (such as `e/` email) do not use `!` as an escape character. Their own validation rules still apply; for example, email addresses containing `!` are not accepted.

### Locating customers by name, phone or policy number: `find`
Finds customers by name keywords, phone prefix or exact policy number, optionally combined.
* Name search is case-insensitive; for example, `hans` matches `Hans`.
* Keyword order does not matter; for example, `Hans Bo` matches `Bo Hans`.
* Unprefixed keywords search names only, including when a keyword contains digits.
* Keywords match the start of any name word; for example, `Han` matches `Hans` and `Bo Hans`.
* Hyphens separate searchable name components; for example, `find Jane` matches `Mary-Jane Tan`.
* Customers with an exact name-word match appear before prefix-only matches. For example, `find John` shows
`John Tan` before `Johnny Lim`. Matching is case-insensitive and considers any name word or keyword.
* Customers tied in match quality retain their stored order. Searching only changes the displayed order;
`list` restores the full list in stored order, while `list n/` and `list c/` apply their respective sorts.
* Full words also match, but middle-of-word and suffix matches do not; for example, `ans` does not match `Hans`.
* Customers matching at least one keyword are returned (an `OR` search); for example, `Hans Bo` returns `Hans Gruber` and `Bo Yang`.
To search by phone number, use `find p/PHONE_PREFIX`, for example `find p/9876` or `find p/+65`.
* Phone searches match the beginning of the phone number, including the complete number.
For example, `find p/9876` matches `98765432`, while `find p/+65` matches `+6591234567`.
* Supply an optional leading `+` followed by one or more digits (`0-9`). A single digit is allowed, and leading zeros
are preserved. Spaces around the prefix are allowed; spaces within it, letters, hyphens, parentheses, other
punctuation, and a `+` anywhere except the beginning are rejected.
* To combine phone and name criteria, use an explicit `n/` field as described below.
Supplying multiple phone prefixes is not supported and produces an error.
* All customers with matching phone numbers are shown in stored order, including customers sharing a number.
A phone-only search replaces the previous search and display sort. Use the displayed indexes for `edit` and `delete`.

Resizes the main window using either a preset or an explicit width and height. The two forms cannot be combined.
* `p/min` sets the app minimum of 880 by 600 pixels.
* `p/med` sets each dimension to two thirds of the current screen's usable area, raised to the app minimum if needed.
* `p/max` fills the current screen's usable area while leaving a 12-pixel margin on every edge.
* `s/` accepts whole-number width and height in pixels, in that order. Neither dimension may be below the app minimum or exceed the current screen's usable area after the edge margins.

The window stays within the usable area of the screen it currently occupies. If that screen cannot fit the app minimum with the edge margins, resizing is rejected. The new size is saved with your preferences when you exit.

InsureConnect automatically saves customer records after a successful `add`, `edit`, `delete`, or `clear` command that changes the records. `delete` and `clear` save only after you confirm them. Failed or cancelled commands, confirmation prompts, and commands that do not change customer records do not save the records. You do not need to save manually.

InsureConnect saves its files relative to the working directory (the directory from which you launch it): customer records are saved to `data/addressbook.json`, and preferences are saved to `preferences.json`. For example, if you run the JAR by its full path while your terminal is in `/home`, the files are `/home/data/addressbook.json` and `/home/preferences.json`, regardless of where the JAR is stored. Launching InsureConnect from different directories uses different records and preferences files. Launch it from the same directory each time to keep using the same records and preferences. The legacy data filename is retained so existing installations continue to load their records. Advanced users are welcome to update data directly by editing `data/addressbook.json`.
Addresses already saved with more than 300 characters are loaded and preserved as-is. The 300-character limit applies to addresses entered with the `add` and `edit` commands.

If your changes make the data file invalid, InsureConnect displays a warning and starts with an empty customer list. The invalid file remains unchanged and cannot be overwritten by add, edit, delete, or clear; commands that attempt to save customer records will fail. To resume saving, close InsureConnect and repair, move, rename, or delete the invalid file before restarting. We recommend making a backup before editing the file.

Furthermore, certain edits can cause InsureConnect to behave in unexpected ways (e.g., if a value entered is outside of the acceptable range). Therefore, edit the data file only if you are confident that you can update it correctly.
### Loading contact files from older versions
Contact files without `createdAt` timestamps load automatically. Their existing
contact details are preserved, and unknown creation dates use
`1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` as a stable fallback for creation-date sorting. This is a
migration value, not the actual creation date. The timestamp is written on the
next successful save; loading alone does not rewrite the file. Existing valid
timestamps are retained. Malformed timestamps and other invalid contact data
still produce a loading warning. Old labels are not converted into policy
numbers: policy numbers must still be valid and unique across contacts.
**Q**: How do I transfer my data to another computer?
**A**: Install the app on the other computer and overwrite the data file it creates with the `data/addressbook.json` file from your previous InsureConnect working directory.
